title: Where Is It? In, On, Under
overview:
Say where a thing is.
In the bag. On the table. Under the chair.
Ask: where is it?
Say there is one, or there are two.
functions: Follow an instruction about where to put a thing
Say there is one thing or there are many
Say there is not any of a thing
Ask a person to sit, stand, come or go
learningPath: Patterns: in, on, under, and there is.
Say where things are. Record it.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 8. Where is it?
Today, six small words. They are important.
Take a book and a bag.
Put the book in the bag.
The book is in the bag. In.
Now put the book on the bag.
The book is on the bag. On.
Now put the book under the bag.
The book is under the bag. Under.
Say them with me. In. On. Under.
Two more. Next to. Behind.
The chair is next to the table.
The bag is behind the door.
And near. The shop is near my house.
Near is not next to. Near is close.
Now the question. Where is my bag?
It is under the table.
Answer with one of the small words.
Last, a new pattern. There is.
There is a chair in this room.
There are four chairs in this room.
One thing: there is.
More than one: there are.
And for nothing: there is no chair.
That is Unit 8. Go and find your things.

grammar.title: In, on, under
grammar.explanation:
Three small words. They say where.
Show all three with a book and a bag.
grammar.rule:
The book is IN the bag.      (inside)
The book is ON the bag.      (on top)
The book is UNDER the bag.   (below)

in + a place:  in the room, in my pocket
on + a surface: on the table, on the floor
grammar.workedExample:
Your keys are inside your coat.
1. Inside means in.
2. The thing is my coat.
3. Say: The keys are in my coat.
4. Now on top of the table: on the table.
5. Now below it: under the table.
grammar.mistake:
Do not use in for a surface.
No: The book is in the table.
Yes: The book is on the table.
grammar.tip: In is inside. On is touching the top.
grammar.practice:
Write in, on or under.
1. The key is ___ my bag.
2. The cup is ___ the table.
3. The shoes are ___ the bed.
4. The money is ___ my pocket.
5. The bag is ___ the floor.
6. The box is ___ the desk.
7. I live ___ a small town.
8. Put the paper ___ the desk.
grammar.answers:
1. in
2. on
3. under
4. in
5. on
6. under
7. in
8. on
Six or more right? You can say where a thing is.

grammar.title: Where is it?
grammar.explanation:
One question for a place.
The answer uses one of the small words.
grammar.rule:
Where is my bag?
It is under the table.

Where are my keys?
They are in your coat.

one thing → Where IS it?
more than one → Where ARE they?
grammar.workedExample:
You cannot find your phone.
1. Ask: Where is my phone?
2. They answer: It is on the chair.
3. Say it back to check: On the chair?
4. Look there.
5. For more than one: Where ARE my keys?
grammar.mistake:
One thing takes is. More than one takes are.
No: Where is my keys?
Yes: Where are my keys?
grammar.tip: Where is for one. Where are for many.
grammar.practice:
Write is or are.
1. Where ___ my bag?
2. Where ___ my keys?
3. Where ___ the door?
4. Where ___ the children?
5. Where ___ your money?
6. Where ___ the chairs?
grammar.answers:
1. is
2. are
3. is
4. are
5. is
6. are
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: There is and there are
grammar.explanation:
This is how English says a thing exists.
One thing: there is.
More than one: there are.
grammar.rule:
There is a chair in this room.
There are four chairs in this room.

There is a shop near here.
There are two shops near here.

Question:  Is there a shop near here?
           Are there any shops?
grammar.workedExample:
You want to say the room has one door.
1. It is one thing.
2. So use there is.
3. Then the thing: a door.
4. Then the place: in this room.
5. Say: There is a door in this room.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say: Here is a chair. That means something else.
There is a chair = a chair exists here.
Here is a chair = I am giving it to you.
grammar.practice:
Write is or are.
1. There ___ a door here.
2. There ___ four chairs.
3. There ___ some water.
4. There ___ two windows.
5. There ___ a shop near here.
6. There ___ many people.
grammar.answers:
1. is
2. are
3. is
4. are
5. is
6. are
Five or six right? This pattern is used every day.

grammar.title: There is no, there are not any
grammar.explanation:
Two ways to say a thing is not there.
Both are correct. Learn one well.
grammar.rule:
There is no bread.
There is not any bread.

There are no chairs.
There are not any chairs.

no + thing
not any + thing
grammar.workedExample:
The shop has finished its milk.
1. Milk is one amount, so use is.
2. Simple way: There is no milk.
3. Other way: There is not any milk.
4. Both are right.
5. In a question, use any: Is there any milk?
grammar.mistake:
Do not use no and not together.
No: There is not no milk.
Yes: There is no milk.
grammar.tip: Use any in questions. Use no in answers.
grammar.practice:
Make it negative.
1. There is some bread. ___
2. There are some chairs. ___
3. There is a shop near here. ___
4. There is some water. ___
5. There are two doors. ___
grammar.answers:
1. There is no bread. / There is not any bread.
2. There are no chairs. / There are not any chairs.
3. There is no shop near here.
4. There is no water.
5. There are no doors.
Four or five right? Good.

readings.title: Where Are My Keys?
readings.genre: A short text about looking for a thing
readings.setting: A small flat, in the morning
readings.passage:
I cannot find my keys.
They are not in my bag.
They are not on the table.
I look under the chair.
They are not there.
I look behind the door.
There they are!
They are in my coat.
Now I can go to work.

readings.title: My Room
readings.setting: A small room with one window
readings.passage:
My room is little.
There is one window.
There is a bed next to the window.
There is a table and a chair.
The table is near the door.
There are no big things.
My bag is under the bed.
My books are on the table.
It is little, but it is enough.

readings.title: Where to Put Things
readings.genre: A sign in a waiting room
readings.setting: A wall in a waiting room
readings.passage:
Put your bag under your chair.
Do not put bags on the chairs.
The toilet is behind this room.
The desk is next to the door.
Please sit and wait.

comprehension.q: What is the person looking for?
comprehension.why: Line 1: I cannot find my keys.

comprehension.a: Not in the bag and not on the table.

comprehension.q: Where does the person look third?
comprehension.why: Line 4: I look under the chair.
Line 8: They are in my coat.
Line 3: There is a bed next to the window.
Line 7: My bag is under the bed.

comprehension.q: Is the room full of things?
comprehension.why: Line 6: There are no big things.

comprehension.q: Where do you put your bag?
comprehension.why: Line 1: Put your bag under your chair.
Line 4: The desk is next to the door.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — In, on, under
speaking.instructions:
Take a book and a bag.
Do each one, then say it.
1. Put the book in the bag. Say: It is in the bag.
2. Put the book on the bag. Say: It is on the bag.
3. Put the book under the bag. Say: It is under the bag.
4. Put the book next to the bag.
5. Put the book behind the bag.
Tap the mic. Say five lines.
Check: did you do it and say it?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor where to put a thing. Do it and say where it is.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Where is it?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Where is my bag? B: It is under the table.
2. A: Where are my keys? B: They are in your coat.
3. A: Where is the toilet? B: It is behind this room.
4. A: Thank you. B: You are welcome.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: it is for one, they are for many?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor where three things are. Answer its questions too.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Do what you hear
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Do the thing.
1. Put your pen on the table.
2. Put your bag under your chair.
3. Open your book.
4. Close your book.
5. Stand up.
6. Sit down.
Do it two times.
Now say each instruction yourself.
Check: did you do each one, not just hear it?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for four instructions. Do each one.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — There is, there are
speaking.instructions:
Look at this room. Say six lines.
1. There is a ___.
2. There is a ___.
3. There are two ___.
4. There are four ___.
5. There is no ___.
6. There are no ___.
Tap the mic. Say the six lines.
Check: is for one, are for many?
speaking.tutor: Describe your room to the tutor. Use there is and there are.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Look at this room. Say six lines.
One. There is a ...
Two. There is a ...
Three. There are two ...
Four. There are four ...
Five. There is no ...
Six. There are no ...
Tap the mic. Say the six lines.
Check: is for one, are for many?

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Find it
speaking.instructions:
A friend cannot find a thing. Help them.
1. A: Where is my phone? B: It is on the chair.
2. A: It is not there. B: Look under the chair.
3. A: Not there. B: Look in your bag.
4. A: Here it is! B: Good.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: a different place each time?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to hide a thing in words. Guess where it is.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The two sounds of th
speaking.instructions:
There and the have a soft th.
Your tongue touches your teeth.
The air comes out with a buzz.
Listen and repeat.
there ... the ... they ... this
Now say these lines.
There is a book on the table.
There are three chairs.
Tap the mic. Say both lines.
Check: is it a buzz, not a d?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say there and dare. Say which one you heard.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Where my things are
writing.prompt:
Write four lines.
Say where four of your things are.
Use a different word each time.
writing.model:
My keys are in my bag.
My phone is on the table.
My shoes are under the bed.
My coat is behind the door.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
A different place word in each one.
Each line starts with a capital.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add one line saying where a thing is NOT.

writing.title: Writing 2 — This room
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about this room.
Use there is and there are.
Say where two of the things are.
writing.model:
There is one window.
There are four chairs.
The table is near the door.
There are no big things.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
There is and there are both used.
At least one line says where a thing is.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line saying what there is NOT in the room.

activities.title: Practice 1 — In, on or under?
activities.instructions:
Write in, on or under.
1. The key is ___ my bag.
2. The cup is ___ the table.
3. The shoes are ___ the bed.
4. The money is ___ my pocket.
5. The bag is ___ the floor.
6. The box is ___ the desk.
7. I live ___ a small town.
8. The paper is ___ the book.
activities.answers:
1. in
2. on
3. under
4. in
5. on
6. under
7. in
8. on (or under)
Six or more right: good.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Where is it?
activities.instructions:
Ask and answer about six things in this room.
Where is the ___? It is ___ the ___.
Use a different place word each time if you can.
activities.answers:
There is no key here.
Check: did you use is for one thing?
Did you use are for more than one?
Did you use more than two different place words?
activities.solo: Record all six, then listen back.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Do it
activities.instructions:
Do each instruction. Then say it out loud.
1. Put your pen on the table.
2. Put your bag under your chair.
3. Open your book.
4. Close the door.
5. Stand up.
6. Sit down.
activities.answers:
There is no written key.
Check: did you do all six?
Could you say each one back afterwards?
Six done and said: you can follow spoken instructions.
activities.solo: Do them alone, then check yourself.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Is or are?
activities.instructions:
Write is or are.
1. There ___ a door.
2. There ___ four chairs.
3. There ___ some water.
4. There ___ two windows.
5. There ___ a shop near here.
6. There ___ many people.
activities.answers:
1. is
2. are
3. is
4. are
5. is
6. are
Five or six right: good.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Say it is not there
activities.instructions:
Make each one negative.
1. There is some bread.
2. There are some chairs.
3. There is a shop near here.
4. There is some water.
5. There are two doors.
activities.answers:
1. There is no bread.
2. There are no chairs.
3. There is no shop near here.
4. There is no water.
5. There are no doors.
Not any is also right in every one.
Four or five right: good.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read and find
activities.instructions:
Read My Room again.
1. How many windows?
2. Where is the bed?
3. Where is the bag?
4. Where are the books?
5. Are there big things?
activities.answers:
1. One
2. Next to the window
3. Under the bed
4. On the table
5. No
Four or five right: you can read a description of a place.
activities.solo: Read it, then answer without looking.

quizzes.q: The key is inside my bag. The key is ___ my bag.
quizzes.why: In means inside. On means touching the top.

quizzes.q: The cup is touching the top of the table. It is ___ the table.
quizzes.why: On is for a surface: on the table.

quizzes.q: The shoes are below the bed. They are ___ the bed.

quizzes.why: Keys is more than one, so are.

quizzes.q: There ___ one door in this room.
There ___ four chairs in this room.
Which one says a thing exists here?
quizzes.why: Here is a chair means you are giving it.

quizzes.q: The shop has finished its bread. There is ___ bread.
quizzes.why: No means none at all. Not any is also right.

quizzes.q: Which word goes in a question? Is there ___ milk?
quizzes.why: Any goes in questions and after not.

quizzes.q: The chair is beside the table, touching it. It is ___ the table.
quizzes.why: Next to means beside, with nothing between.

quizzes.q: The garden is at the back of the house. It is ___ the house.
quizzes.why: Behind means at the back of.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: Teach this with objects, not pictures
teacherNotes.note: In, on and under are the easiest words in the language to demonstrate and the hardest to explain. A book and a bag will do the whole unit. A learner who has put the book in, on and under the bag with their own hands does not need a translation.

teacherNotes.type: There is and there are is a pattern, not a word
teacherNotes.note: It is how English says something exists, and no single word in the learner's own language matches it. Expect it to take longer than the prepositions. Pattern 3 and Practice 4 are the ones to come back to.
Next to means touching or almost. Near means somewhere close. Learners collapse them and it matters when they are giving directions, which is Unit 13.
Keys, shoes and glasses are always plural in English and learners regularly say where is my keys. Point at the s. It is a two-second correction that lasts.

assignment.title: Where everything is
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say where six of your things are.
Use in, on, under, next to and behind.
2. Write four lines about this room.
Use there is and there are.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
